title: Equality case for majority singleton coefficients
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Define majority to be $+1$ when the sum of the coordinates is nonnegative and $-1$ otherwise. The sum of the singleton Fourier coefficients of $f$ equals that of majority if and only if $f(x)$ agrees with majority at every $x$ whose coordinate sum is nonzero.
